subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper marked an article at ₹5,000. The shopkeeper allows successive discounts of 20%, 15% and 10%. The selling price of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given percentage discounts into multiplying fractions: 20% = 4/5, 15% = 17/20, 10% = 9/10.

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price × (Fraction 1) × (Fraction 2) × (Fraction 3)

SP = 5000 × 4/5 × 17/20 × 9/10

SP = 5000 × 612/1000 = 3060

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,060.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹5,000

Successive discounts = 20%, 15% and 10%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d904b7c1afec448f5252dd375de5a2d2ce01f58e3a57d9310f4edb027e7cd41c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100) × (1 − D₃/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 5000 × (1 − 20/100) × (1 − 15/100) × (1 − 10/100)

⇒ SP = 5000 × (80/100) × (85/100) × (90/100)

⇒ SP = 5000 × (4/5) × (17/20) × (9/10)

⇒ SP = 5000 × (612/1000)

⇒ SP = 5 × 612

⇒ SP = 3060

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,060.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Single Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is given by (a + b − a×b/100)%.

Marked Price and Cost Price Relationship

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be directly calculated using: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer pretends to sell goods at cost price but uses a false weight, the actual profit percentage is found using: Profit% = [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100%.
